title: anticipatory-resize-policy-and-tenant-throttle-fence
author: Maya Thompson
description: Context: customer fleets have become sensitive to repeated rapid scale-in events that withdraw headroom too aggressively, causing short-lived saturation and increased tail latency. Motivation: reduce oscillation during transient drops while preserving the ability to grant short-term burst capacity when warranted. This PR adds an "anticipatory resize" policy that delays scale-in decisions based on a saturation-aware prediction window, and a tenant-level "throttle fence" that serializes competing credit reconciliations to avoid double-counting burst capacity. Design summary: 1) Anticipatory resize: a lightweight moving-window predictor samples per-tenant utilization percentiles (P50/P95), current queue depth, and warm-pool fill ratio to compute a short horizon demand estimate. Rather than immediately reducing shard counts when utilization dips, the controller enters a guarded cooldown that only commits scale-in if the prediction window remains below the target for a configured grace period. This is configurable via autoscaler policy fields: anticipatory.enabled (bool), anticipatory.window_seconds (int), anticipatory.grace_seconds (int), anticipatory.saturation_threshold (float). 2) Throttle fence: reconciler-level fencing around burst-credit reconciliation ensures only one in-flight reconciliation per tenant/fleet pair; this prevents two concurrent controllers (e.g. during leader handover or canary) from both deducting the same soft burst credits and oversubscribing. Fence semantics are optimistic-lease-based with a short TTL to avoid permanent locks during failover. 3) Saturation-aware backfill: when a short-term deficit is detected, the reconciler will prefer backfill from the warm-pool and deferred soft credits before hard provisioning, and will emit a new telemetry dimension (reconciled_burst_source) describing whether capacity came from warm-pool, deferred_credit, or new_provision. Rollout strategy: feature gated behind OPT_IN policy flag; default off for existing clusters. We perform a staged rollout: first enable on the perf-canary cluster with a single canary tenant, then ramp to 10% of traffic with metrics baseline checks, then full rollout if no regression. Backwards compatibility: controllers that don't support anticipatory fields will ignore them. Implementation notes: - Introduced pkg/autoscaler/policy/anticipatory_resize.go: core scheduler logic and unit tests. - Introduced pkg/autoscaler/allocator/throttle_fence.go: fencing primitives and lease renewal helpers. - Added metrics: autoscaler_anticipatory_decision_count, autoscaler_anticipatory_abort_reason, reconciled_burst_source (labels: tenant, fleet, source). - Config changes: chart value anticipatory.enabled=false by default; helm values and example configs updated. - Tests: new unit tests and an end-to-end stability test (test/e2e/resize_stability_test.go) with a deterministic workload generator to validate cooldown logic. Benchmarks: bench/scale_sweep.md includes a throughput/latency sweep demonstrating reduction in scale-in churn (observed 37% fewer scale-ins and 12% lower 99p tail latency on canary). Security/ops: lease-based fences limit risk of deadlocks and provide observability hooks for stuck fences. Migration/upgrade: rolling upgrade safe; the fence uses a short TTL so mixed-version clusters behave conservatively (no double-reconciliation).

review_comments: Arjun Patel: The predictor uses a moving average over P50/P95 and queue depth—can you add a short note on numerical stability and upper-bound clamps?

Sofia Delgado: Throttle fence looks good but we need a clear operational playbook for stuck leases—please add an alert rule.

Maya Thompson: Switched the test to deterministically seed the generator and increased grace_seconds in test harness to remove timing flakiness; CI was green after this change.
ci_checks: unit-tests: failed -> fixed (race condition in lease renewal)
release_notes: Added anticipatory resize policy (opt-in) to reduce scale-in oscillations; added tenant throttle fence to avoid concurrent burst-credit reconciliation; new metrics: autoscaler_anticipatory_decision_count, autoscaler_anticipatory_abort_reason, reconciled_burst_source. Opt-in via charts.redwood-autoscaler.values: anticipatory.enabled=false by default.
merge_notes: Squash-merged after sign-off from reviewers. Canary run validated decreased churn; rollout scheduled and feature gated by default off.
additional_context: Related to ENG-8721 (stabilize fleet headroom under transient drops). Incident SUP-3387 drove the urgent need to prevent dual reconciliation during leader failover. This approach favors safety over aggressive immediate deallocation and gives operators visibility into short-term backfills.
user_impact_summary: No change for default clusters (opt-in). Customers enabling the anticipatory policy should observe fewer rapid scale-ins during bursty workloads and improved 99p latency, at the cost of a slightly longer cooldown before scale-in completes. Throttle fence reduces instances of oversubscription caused by concurrent reconciliations.
notes_for_ops: If you see autoscaler.fence_stuck alerts, check fence_lease_owner and restart the reconciler if owner is non-responsive. To roll back, set charts.redwood-autoscaler.values: anticipatory.enabled=false and helm upgrade; the system will gradually resume previous behavior.
post_merge_actions: 1) Enable on perf-canary tenant (ops). 2) Watch reconciled_burst_source and autoscaler_anticipatory_decision_count dashboards for 48 hours. 3) If metrics stable, increase rollout to 10% and run load sweeps. 4) Document any field tuning in ENG-8954.
example_config_snippet: anticipatory: { enabled: false, window_seconds: 30, grace_seconds: 45, saturation_threshold: 0.65 }
